name: Alpine APK
auth: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.
fresh_home: Create a new AW_WORK with mktemp -d for every run; client configuration, downloads and caches in the commands stay under this directory. Do not reuse it to prove a fresh download. Remove the temporary directory after use.
prerequisites: An existing Alpine repository and a signed x86_64 APK named hello at 1.0-r0.
Trusted public keys for both the package and repository index.
apk-tools 3 supports --usermode; run inside the pinned container for a reproducible client.

configure.code:
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/keys"
AW_AUTH_URL=$(python3 - <<'PYCODE'
import os
from urllib.parse import quote, urlsplit, urlunsplit
u = urlsplit(os.environ["AW_URL"])
auth = quote(os.environ["AW_USER"], safe="") + ":" + quote(os.environ["AW_TOKEN"], safe="")
print(urlunsplit((u.scheme, auth + "@" + u.netloc, u.path, "", "")))
PYCODE
)
printf '%s\n' "$AW_AUTH_URL/artifactory/$AW_REPO/v3.20/main" > "$AW_WORK/repositories"
configure.note: Run in the pinned Alpine environment with Python 3 available for URL encoding, or create the 0600 repositories file using equivalent URL-safe credentials. v3.20 is the example repository branch, independent of the client image version.
Obtain and verify the repository/package signing public key from the operator. The filename alias must match the signatures; the fixture uses test.rsa.pub.

publish.note: Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

steps.note: Publish an already signed APK; the repository needs its primary signing key configured so it can sign APKINDEX.tar.gz.

install.note: Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

steps.note: Installs into a temporary root and verifies the signed index and package. Do not disable signature checks.

limitations: Federated proof covers one node. Branch, component and architecture are part of the URL; adapt all three together.

contains: apk installs from a signed <class> repository
